title: Correction Basis for Entries on the Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
An entry on a Keyturn Host Payout Account that was wrong is put right by a correcting entry naming the entry it corrects, and the original entry is never edited, so the statement always shows what happened and what was done about it.

## The window a correction may be made in

A correction may be made inside the schedule's adjustment window counted in whole calendar days from the day the original entry was booked, and an entry older than that window is not corrected on the account but dealt with as a goodwill payment instead. The comparison is not later than the end of that window, and the last day of the window itself satisfies it.

Take a hypothetical entry booked on an account whose schedule sets a window of 60 calendar days. Counted from the day that entry was booked, the sixtieth day is still inside the window and the correction may be made on it; on the sixty-first day the entry is no longer corrected on the account and is dealt with as a goodwill payment instead.

What fixes the day is the original entry's own record: the day it was booked, its own reference number and the basis it was booked on. The correcting entry is booked against that reference number, and the position is read before the correction is made.

## The ceiling on a correction

A correction above the schedule's adjustment ceiling is not made by the service desk at all and goes to the settlements team, whatever the host says about the amount.

## What a correction is and is not

A correction never moves money out of the account; where money is to be sent it is a transfer, and where money is to be taken it is a deduction.

## A clause no longer in force

One clause of this correction basis has been withdrawn and is no longer in force; it is not applied:

> "Money reaching the account from a claim settlement is booked as a correction on its own basis, so that claim money and trip money never appear as the same kind of entry."

superseded_clauses: Money reaching the account from a claim settlement is booked as a correction on its own basis, so that claim money and trip money never appear as the same kind of entry.
